You do not need to buy a course, open a playing account or finish a reading list to begin. Learn standard no-limit Texas hold’em through one guided hand and six connected stages. Start small, explain a fresh example, then choose the next step. Do one scene or one first-pass lesson, then pause. The reading estimate covers all the explanations and the printable card, rather than the time needed for a single visit. Prefer an overview before practicing? Read the complete beginner Hold’em guide in parts. The foundation lessons offer smaller questions; the long guide connects rules, prices and strategic ideas in one place. Planning to try a game? The first-session guide connects format, full cost, procedure and a first-month practice plan. Start with its no-wager practice options .

The guided hand below introduces the action, shared cards and pot in six scenes. Each scene explains an answer and offers a precise repair link. Prefer to read first? Open the first lesson and use its first-pass guide.

Use counters or paper. The actions are scripted to explain the rules and accounting; they are not betting recommendations. Read a scene, give your reason, then compare it with the explanation. You can continue after any answer. Skip to the six-stage lesson map . No account or wager is needed. Six scenes, from the first action to the result.

Six players start with 100 counters each. The small blind posts 1 and the big blind posts 2. There is no ante, fee or side pot. Three players fold. You are on the button, the seat marked by the dealer marker. Both blinds still have their first decisions. First seat: folded Next seat: folded Cutoff: folded Button: you Small blind: posted 1 Big blind: posted 2 Your private cards Shared board No shared cards yet. Pot now 3 Your stack behind 100 Big blind behind 98 After your initial action on the button, who still has an initial decision? Nobody; the flop must come next. The small blind and the big blind. Only the big blind. Say your answer and the reason, then reveal the explanation.

For this scripted practice hand, you raise to 6 total and the small blind folds. The big blind already posted 2 on this betting round and faces your total wager of 6. The current pot is your 6, the folded small blind's 1 and the big blind's 2: 9. Your private cards Shared board No shared cards yet.
